upright: The Moon lights the world in a way that distorts shapes and hides detail. When it appears, things may not be what they seem. Uncertainty, mixed signals, and half-seen facts can make it difficult to know what to trust. Dreams, fears, and old memories may surface, and imagination can run wild. The dog and wolf represent tamed and untamed instincts, both responding to the same light. The path leads ahead between the towers, a reminder that you can keep moving even when visibility is poor. Rather than forcing quick conclusions, gather information slowly and be careful about decisions based on anxiety or assumption. Pay attention to your intuition, but test it against what you can verify. Keep a dream journal, talk to someone you trust, and notice recurring emotions. The card asks you to be patient with confusion and to respect the subconscious, which carries valuable material. Light will return, and what looks threatening in shadow may look quite different by day.
reversed: Reversed, The Moon suggests that fog is beginning to lift. Confusion is clearing, hidden facts are emerging, and fears that seemed enormous may be shrinking when examined. You might be releasing anxiety or recognizing a misunderstanding. It can also indicate that you have been hiding from something and are now ready to face it. In some readings, the reversed card warns of deception or of letting fear and worry grow unchecked, especially if you have been avoiding the truth about a situation. Check for projection, where your own insecurities color how you read someone else. Bring uncertainty into the open by asking direct questions and seeking facts. Look after your sleep and mental wellbeing, as anxiety can distort perception. As clarity returns, act on what you now see rather than on old assumptions.
love: In love, The Moon upright suggests mixed signals, uncertainty, or a connection with hidden depths. Emotions run high and may be hard to read. Avoid assuming the worst and ask questions. Reversed, it points to confusion clearing, secrets surfacing, or anxiety easing. Honest communication helps separate fear from fact. Give feelings time to settle before reacting, and check assumptions directly with the person involved. Try not to read too much into silence.
career: At work, The Moon indicates unclear information, shifting situations, or intuition that needs checking. Avoid major decisions until details are clear. Creative and imaginative work may flourish. Reversed, it suggests clarity arriving, or office rumors and deception. Verify what you hear and trust what can be confirmed. Pay attention to unspoken currents without leaping to conclusions. Write down questions and get clear answers.
finances: Financially, The Moon advises caution when information is incomplete, since things may not be as they appear. Avoid risky deals built on assumptions. Reversed, it suggests that hidden facts are emerging or fears are easing. Review the numbers carefully and rely on evidence, not worry. Wait until the facts are available before deciding.
health: For wellbeing, The Moon relates to sleep, dreams, emotional sensitivity, and anxiety that may rise at night. Calming routines and talking with someone can help. Reversed, it may show anxiety easing or needing attention. This is reflective guidance, not medical advice; consult a qualified professional if worry is persistent.
advice: Move carefully while the picture is unclear, and check your fears against the facts. Clarity will come with time.
as_feelings: Someone feeling The Moon toward you may have emotions that are strong but confusing, even to them. They may be unsure, secretive, or sending mixed signals. Reversed, their feelings may be becoming clearer, or they may be anxious and imagining problems.

name: The Sun
summary: The Sun brings joy, vitality, and clarity. Explore its upright and reversed meanings in love, career, finances, and health.
imagery: A large radiant sun with a human face shines in a clear sky over a garden wall lined with tall sunflowers. A joyful child sits bareback on a white horse, arms wide open, holding a long red banner. The child wears only a red feather in the hair. The scene is bright and uncomplicated, expressing warmth, innocence, and happiness shared without reservation.
upright: The Sun is among the most positive cards in the deck. It brings warmth, clarity, and a sense of things going well. After the uncertainty of the Moon, light floods the scene and everything is visible. You may feel more energetic, confident, and open, and others may respond to your good mood. Success may be near, whether it is a result of hard work, a hopeful project, or simply the satisfaction of living honestly. The child on the horse shows a joy that is natural and unselfconscious. When the card appears, allow yourself to enjoy what is going well without waiting for the other shoe to drop. Share your happiness, spend time outdoors, and do what lights you up. Clarity may also arrive on a question that has been confusing. Make decisions with confidence, but stay grounded. The Sun supports vitality, creativity, and generosity. Let yourself be seen, celebrate small and large wins, and carry some of this brightness into the days that follow.
reversed: Reversed, The Sun suggests the light is partly blocked. Joy may feel muted, enthusiasm may be low, or a hoped-for success may take longer than expected. This is usually a temporary cloud, not a lasting darkness. You may also be overly optimistic, ignoring practical issues in your eagerness, or feeling that you must keep a cheerful face when you do not. Burnout can dim even the brightest energy, so check whether you have been overextending. Look for what is draining your warmth and make small changes: rest, time outdoors, contact with encouraging people, and honest rest from demands. Celebrate modest progress rather than waiting for a grand triumph. If you feel persistently low, consider seeking support. The sun is still there behind the clouds. Allow yourself to feel what you feel, stay patient, and expect that the brighter days you are waiting for will arrive in time.
love: In love, The Sun upright suggests happiness, openness, and a warm, honest connection. It can mark a joyful relationship, a celebration, or the enjoyment of simple time together. If single, you may radiate confidence. Reversed, it points to dampened enthusiasm or unrealistic expectations. Share how you feel and keep expectations reasonable. Laughter, honesty, and shared pleasure are favored. Let yourself be open and enjoy the warmth that is there. Simple time together, outdoors or at home, may feed the bond more than anything elaborate.
career: At work, The Sun suggests success, recognition, and energy that brings projects to life. Your confidence may inspire others. Clear communication pays off. Reversed, it indicates delays, tiredness, or overconfidence. Check your plans for blind spots and pace yourself so you do not burn out. Share credit generously, and let your enthusiasm lead teams. Visible progress may come more easily than usual.
finances: Financially, The Sun points to improving prospects, rewards for effort, and a sense of security. Enjoy gains while keeping sensible habits. Reversed, it warns of overoptimism or delayed returns. Review your numbers realistically and avoid assuming everything will work out without planning. Celebrate progress but keep a buffer, and let steady habits, not optimism alone, carry the gains forward.
health: For wellbeing, The Sun encourages time outdoors, movement, laughter, and activities that bring joy. Energy and mood may be on the rise. Reversed, it may show low energy or overexertion. This is reflective guidance, not medical advice; consult a qualified professional for any health concern.
advice: Let yourself enjoy what is going well and share it. Honest warmth is its own reward.
as_feelings: Someone feeling The Sun toward you is happy around you and wants to be open. Their affection is warm, sincere, and easy to read. Reversed, their enthusiasm may be dampened, or they may be feeling more than they are showing.

name: Judgement
summary: Judgement is about awakening, reflection, and answering a deeper call. Learn its upright and reversed meanings in love, career, finances, and wellbeing.
imagery: An angel, identified with Gabriel, blows a trumpet from the clouds, carrying a flag marked with a cross. Below, men, women, and children rise from coffins on a stormy sea, arms outstretched toward the sound. Snowy mountains tower in the background. The people are gray and unclothed, looking up with open faces. The scene echoes the resurrection and speaks of being called to a new level of awareness.
upright: Judgement is a card of awakening. A trumpet sounds, and the figures below rise, answering a call that asks them to see their lives clearly. When it appears, you may be reviewing your past, understanding what it has taught you, and preparing to step into something new. Despite the name, this is less about being judged by others than about how you assess yourself. It encourages honest reflection, forgiveness, and a willingness to leave behind what no longer fits. You may feel a sense of purpose or a call to change direction, sometimes after a period of difficulty. Listen to it. Make peace with earlier choices, acknowledge what you have learned, and decide who you want to be going forward. If there is someone to forgive, including yourself, consider doing so. The card also reminds you that you are allowed a fresh start. Respond to the call with openness, and bring the lessons of the past with you instead of the weight of it.
reversed: Reversed, Judgement suggests that you are avoiding the call or dwelling in self-criticism. You may be replaying old mistakes, judging yourself harshly, or doubting whether you deserve a second chance. Alternatively, you may be ignoring a clear sense that it is time to change, making excuses to stay as you are. The lessons of the past can go unlearned if you refuse to look at them honestly, and regret can harden into a habit. Try a kinder form of review: what happened, what did it teach, and what would you do differently now? Distinguish genuine responsibility from unfair self-blame. Talk to someone you trust if the past feels heavy. If a decision or calling keeps returning, ask what you fear about answering it. You cannot change what has happened, but you can choose what you do next. Forgiveness, for yourself and others, can make that choice lighter.
love: In love, Judgement upright suggests a reawakening, a second chance, or an honest reckoning that clears the way for a deeper connection. Forgiveness plays a part. Reversed, it points to lingering guilt, harsh self-judgment, or avoiding an important conversation. Reflect on what the past has taught you before you move forward. If an old relationship returns, ask what has genuinely changed. Honest reflection will show whether a fresh start is real.
career: At work, Judgement signals a calling, a career reassessment, or an evaluation that leads to a new stage. You may feel ready to pursue more meaningful work. Reversed, it suggests self-doubt, ignoring a calling, or fear of review. Reflect honestly, learn from the past, and take the next step with confidence. Consider what your work is asking of you, and whether it fits who you have become.
finances: Financially, Judgement suggests a sober review of your money habits and a decision to start fresh. Learn from earlier mistakes without shame. Reversed, it may indicate avoiding a financial reckoning or dwelling on past errors. Make an honest assessment, then set a clear plan for the future. Face your numbers without self-blame.
health: For wellbeing, Judgement can indicate a wake-up moment about your habits and a decision to care for yourself differently. Compassionate self-review helps. Reversed, it may show harsh self-criticism. This is reflective guidance, not medical advice; consult a qualified professional for health concerns.
advice: Review the past with honesty and kindness, then answer the call forward. You are allowed a fresh start.
as_feelings: Someone feeling Judgement toward you is having a realization about their feelings and may be ready to act on them. They could be reflecting honestly and open to a second chance. Reversed, they may be critical of themselves, unsure, or avoiding a decision.

name: The World
summary: The World marks completion, achievement, and wholeness. Discover its upright and reversed meanings in love, career, finances, and health.
imagery: A dancing figure, draped in a flowing purple scarf, floats inside a large green laurel wreath tied with red ribbons. Each hand holds a wand. In the four corners are the winged man, eagle, lion, and bull, the same figures seen on the Wheel of Fortune. The scene is balanced and circular, showing a cycle completed and everything in its place.
upright: The World is the last of the Major Arcana, and it signals completion. A cycle has reached its natural end, and you may be standing in a moment of achievement, integration, and well-earned satisfaction. Goals long in progress may come to fruition, whether a degree, a project, a move, or a personal change. The dancer within the wreath is at ease, holding the wands loosely. She has what she needs and moves with it. When the card appears, take time to recognize how far you have come and appreciate the lessons that brought you here. Wholeness does not mean perfection, only that the parts of your experience are fitting together. It can also point to travel, wider horizons, or feeling at home in the world. Celebrate, then be ready for the next step, because the end of one cycle makes room for another. Carry your accumulated experience forward and let this moment of fulfillment give you confidence for whatever you begin next.
reversed: Reversed, The World suggests that something is not yet complete. You may be close to a goal but stuck on the last step, or you may feel a lack of closure about a situation, a relationship, or a phase of life. Perhaps you are avoiding finishing because the next stage feels uncertain. Delays and loose ends can leave a sense of being incomplete, even when most of the work is done. Identify what remains: a conversation, a piece of paperwork, a decision, or a feeling that needs acknowledgment. Small actions toward closure can ease the sense of drift. If you are chasing a result that never feels like enough, consider whether you are measuring success fairly. Allow yourself to appreciate what you have accomplished along the way. When you finish what you started, or consciously release what cannot be finished, you free energy for what comes next.
love: In love, The World upright suggests fulfillment, a mature and whole partnership, or arriving at a lasting commitment. If single, you may feel complete on your own and ready for a connection that adds to your life. Reversed, it points to loose ends, missing closure, or a relationship that feels almost but not quite settled. Take time to savor the connection and name what you have built. Wholeness often comes when you appreciate each other as you are.
career: At work, The World signals achievement, completion of a major project, and recognition of your effort. Opportunities may broaden, including international ones. Reversed, it suggests delays, unfinished tasks, or lack of closure. Identify the final steps and complete them, or deliberately choose to move on. Celebrate the finish, document what you learned, and consider where to aim next. Thank the people who helped you reach this point, since they may be part of what comes after.
finances: Financially, The World points to reaching a goal, stability, and the reward of long-term planning. You may feel secure about your position. Reversed, it suggests delayed results or loose ends in financial matters. Tie up outstanding details and set your next target when the current one is done. Take stock of your achievement, then choose your next goal.
health: For wellbeing, The World suggests harmony between body, mind, and surroundings, and satisfaction in reaching a personal health goal. Reversed, it may show a plateau or an incomplete process. This is reflective guidance, not medical advice; consult a qualified professional for health concerns.
advice: Acknowledge how far you have come, then finish what remains. A completed cycle leaves room for the next.
as_feelings: Someone feeling The World toward you feels whole, content, and sees real potential in the relationship. They may regard you as part of a complete picture. Reversed, they may feel something is unfinished, unresolved, or not quite ready for the next stage.

name: Ace of Wands
summary: A fresh surge of energy and inspiration arrives, inviting you to act on an idea while the spark is still warm.
imagery: A hand emerges from a cloud and grips a sturdy wooden staff that is sprouting green leaves. Some leaves drift through the air below. Beneath the hand, a quiet river valley, a distant castle on a hilltop and rolling mountains stretch out in soft light. The sprouting wood shows life still growing, and the cloud suggests this gift comes from beyond your own planning. The offering is held out to you, and the choice to take it belongs to you.
upright: The Ace of Wands marks the moment a new idea catches fire. You may feel a rush of motivation, a clear urge to start something, or a sense that your energy has finally come back after a flat stretch. This is raw potential rather than a finished plan, and that is its charm. The staff in the card is already sprouting, which suggests that life is ready to grow if you give it attention. You might be drawn toward a creative project, a business idea, a move, a new hobby or simply a bolder way of living. Pay attention to what excites you without being asked. That is usually where this card points. It does not promise results, and the spark can fade if you leave it sitting. The invitation is to take one small, real step soon, while the feeling is strong. Passion works best when it gets a direction, even a rough one. Trust the enthusiasm, then give it some structure so it can last.
reversed: Reversed, the Ace of Wands often describes a spark that struggles to catch. You may have ideas but feel unable to start, or you started with energy and watched it drain away within days. You may be running on empty and mistaking a lack of fuel for a lack of desire. Other times, fear of failing keeps the idea safely in your head where it cannot be judged. The card can also point to bad timing, a delayed project, or an opportunity that arrives in a form you are not ready for. Look at what is draining you, whether it is overcommitment, criticism or a lack of rest, and see what can be eased. Choose one modest action instead of waiting for a burst of inspiration. Motivation sometimes follows movement rather than preceding it, so a small start may be enough to warm things up again.
love: In love, the Ace of Wands suggests a spark of attraction or renewed excitement. If you are single, you may meet someone who makes you feel lively and curious, and the early connection could feel immediate. In a relationship, it can point to fresh passion, a new shared adventure or a return of playfulness after a quiet period. Let the warmth be real without rushing to define it. Flirt, make plans, try something new together. Reversed, it may hint at flat chemistry or a hesitant start that needs patience.
career: At work, this card points to a new opportunity, a project that excites you, or the energy to pursue a change you have been considering. It can show up when you are offered a role with room to grow or when your own idea begins to feel workable. Act on it with some preparation, because enthusiasm alone rarely finishes a project. Reversed, you may face delays, unclear goals or a stalled pitch that needs more groundwork.
finances: Financially, the Ace of Wands can signal a new source of income, a promising venture or the motivation to start a savings plan. It favours beginnings more than guarantees, so keep your decisions measured. Test an idea on a small scale before committing large sums. Reversed, it may warn of a plan that has not been thought through or a payoff that takes longer than hoped.
health: For your wellbeing, this card suggests a renewed burst of vitality and a desire to move. It can be a good moment to begin a gentle routine such as walking, stretching or dancing. Reversed, you may be running low and could benefit from rest. If you have worries about your health, speak with a professional.
advice: Act on the spark in a small way today, before doubt gets a chance to talk you out of it. Let the first step be simple and real.
as_feelings: They may feel a lively pull toward you, with energy and curiosity in the mix. There could be a wish to start something and see where it goes. It may still be early and unformed, so their interest might show up as enthusiasm more than a settled plan.

name: Two of Wands
summary: You stand with the first win behind you, weighing what to do next and which direction deserves your energy.
imagery: A figure in a rich red tunic stands on the battlements of a castle, holding a small globe in one hand while the other rests on a tall wooden staff. A second staff is fixed to the wall beside them. Below, the sea meets a green landscape with hills and a few small fields. The globe shows the whole world in the palm of a hand, and the figure is looking outward rather than at the walls that protect them, as if the next step has not yet been chosen.
upright: The Two of Wands shows you at a crossroads of comfort and curiosity. You have already built something, whether it is a skill, a position, a home or a bit of confidence, and now you wonder what lies beyond it. The figure on the wall is safe, yet gazes at the horizon, which suggests that safety alone is no longer enough. This card often appears when you are planning, researching or deciding which path to take. Take time to look at the whole picture instead of the nearest option, and be honest about what you want. It asks you to think with ambition and clarity, to draft the plan and test it against your values. A decision made with your eyes open will carry more strength than one made from restlessness. When the choice feels right, you can move from the wall to the road with real purpose.
reversed: Reversed, the Two of Wands can show hesitation that has gone on too long. You may have a plan but keep rewriting it, or you may avoid looking at the horizon because the unknown feels unsettling. There can be a pull to stay in a familiar spot even though part of you wants more. It can also suggest that you are holding yourself back through comparison, waiting for a perfect moment that never arrives. Ask yourself what exactly you are afraid of, and whether the fear is about a real risk or just about change. A small pilot step might help, such as a conversation or a trial run, which lets you test your plan without committing everything.
love: In love, the Two of Wands suggests you are deciding how much you want from a relationship, or what kind of partner or life you wish to build. In a partnership, it may mean planning a shared future, perhaps a move, travel or a major change. If you are single, you might be picky for good reasons or considering a connection across distance. Think about what you really want, then share it. Reversed, indecision or fear of commitment may be getting in the way.
career: At work, this card shows planning, vision and the early look at a bigger role. You may be weighing a promotion, a new venture or a move abroad. Gather information, speak to people who have done it and set a realistic timeline. You have enough footing to aim higher. Reversed, you might be stuck in analysis, afraid to leave a stable job, or working with plans that need more detail.
finances: Financially, the Two of Wands encourages you to plan ahead. This is a good moment to review budgets, think about investments or consider what long-term goals deserve your savings. You are in a position to choose, so choose with some care. Reversed, you may be overly cautious, or you may be skipping the research that would make a decision safer.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests looking at the bigger picture of your habits and setting goals you care about. Think about what kind of lifestyle you want a year from now and plan small steps toward it. Reversed, you may feel stuck in old routines. Speak to a professional if you want tailored guidance.
advice: Write down where you want to be in a year and name one concrete step toward it. Let your plan be ambitious and specific.
as_feelings: They may be thinking about the future and where you fit in it. Part of them could be considering options and not yet ready to commit. Their interest may be sincere, but they might be weighing timing, distance or other plans before they act.

name: Three of Wands
summary: Your plans are in motion and the first results are on the horizon, so patience and a wider view will serve you well.
imagery: A figure in a green cloak stands with their back to us on a rocky ledge, one hand resting on a tall staff planted in the ground. Two more staffs stand upright on either side. Before them, a calm sea stretches toward distant mountains, and several ships sail across the water beneath a warm yellow sky. The posture shows someone who has done the groundwork and now watches their efforts travel outward, trusting that what was sent will return.
upright: The Three of Wands often arrives when you have already taken action and are waiting to see what happens. The ships on the water are the plans, offers or ideas you set in motion, and the figure watching them shows a mix of confidence and patience. This card carries a sense of growth and wider horizons. It can point to opportunities beyond your usual circle, including travel, long-distance work, collaboration with people far away or simply a larger sense of what is possible. You are no longer at the starting line. The foundation exists, and now the effort lies in guiding things outward. Think ahead about the next stage, and avoid letting yourself be surprised by success or delay. Keep an eye on the horizon but also tend to your lines of communication, since news may come from afar. This is a hopeful card that favours foresight. You may not yet see the full result, yet the direction seems promising.
reversed: Reversed, the Three of Wands can describe ships that are late, lost or sailing in the wrong direction. You may feel frustrated by delays, by an answer that never comes, or by the sense that your efforts have not been noticed. Sometimes the cause is a lack of foresight, such as a plan that missed an important detail or an assumption that turned out wrong. At other times, the obstacle sits outside your control, like a slow response or an unexpected change in the market. Try not to take it as a sign that the whole idea was mistaken. Check where the plan could be tightened, and consider whether you have communicated clearly with those involved. It may help to prepare a second route in case the first stalls. Impatience can push you to withdraw too early, so make a calm assessment before you do.
love: In love, the Three of Wands suggests a connection that is expanding. A long-distance bond, someone from a different background or a relationship that is moving into a larger shared life may be in view. If you are single, you could meet someone through travel or work, or after you step outside your usual circles. Be patient while things develop. Reversed, distance or poor timing may cause frustration and mixed signals.
career: At work, this card points to growth, foresight and results beginning to come in. Expansion into new markets, international contacts or a role with a wider reach may be possible. You have laid a foundation, so keep communication open. Reversed, expect delays, a project stalling or a plan that did not account for every factor. Review and adjust. Keep your goals visible.
finances: Financially, the Three of Wands suggests investments or efforts beginning to bear fruit, perhaps with income from further afield. Keep planning ahead and avoid assuming success is immediate. Reversed, returns may be slow or a venture may not have been planned well, so review your numbers and expectations calmly. Stay patient.
health: For wellbeing, this card favours taking a longer view of your habits and being patient with results. Changes you have started may need time to show. A walk with wide views could help you feel more settled. Reversed, you may feel discouraged by slow progress. Consult a professional for guidance.
advice: Keep your plans moving and your eyes on the horizon. Trust that effort already given may be on its way back to you.
as_feelings: They may be looking at you with a long view, seeing what a future could hold. There could be interest tied to distance, travel or a wider life. They might be waiting to see how things develop before showing more.

name: Four of Wands
summary: A happy milestone or gathering brings stability, harmony and a deserved moment to celebrate what you have built.
imagery: Four tall wooden staffs stand at the corners of a canopy decorated with a garland of flowers and fruit. Beneath it, two figures raise bouquets in a joyful gesture. In the background, a castle sits across a moat, and a crowd of people gathers to celebrate or dance. The sky is pale and bright. Everything in the picture feels open and shared, from the garland to the distant guests, suggesting a hard-earned foundation that now welcomes others in.
upright: The Four of Wands is one of the warmest cards in the deck. It speaks of milestones and the happiness of reaching a safe, steady place after effort. You might see a wedding, a housewarming, a family reunion, a graduation or a project finished with people who helped you do it. Beyond the literal events, it describes the feeling that you belong, that your foundations are solid, and that others are glad to share in your progress. The four staffs create a structure that supports the celebration, a reminder that joy tends to feel best when there is a framework beneath it. This card encourages you to pause and enjoy what you have achieved before moving on to the next goal. It also points to harmony in your home, workplace or community, and the ease of working with people who share your values. Allow yourself to be glad without waiting for a perfect outcome. If there is an occasion to mark, mark it, and let others share it with you.
reversed: Reversed, the Four of Wands may suggest that the celebration feels out of reach or that the ground beneath your home or community is shaky. You may feel unwelcome somewhere, disconnected from the people around you, or unsure that a recent success is stable. Plans for a gathering could be postponed, or tension might be hiding beneath a cheerful surface. The card can also show conflict between family members or colleagues, or a sense of living in a place that does not feel like home. Look at where the foundation needs strengthening before asking more from it. Honest conversations are better than polite silence. If you feel alone, consider reaching out first, since belonging often begins with an invitation.
love: In love, the Four of Wands suggests a happy, stable stage. It can point to an engagement, moving in together, introducing a partner to family or simply feeling at home with someone. If you are single, social gatherings may be where you connect with someone. Enjoy the warmth and let people celebrate with you. Reversed, there may be tension about commitment, family or where you belong together. Warmth grows with attention.
career: At work, this card signals a milestone worth marking, such as a completed project, a good team atmosphere or a stable position. It favours collaboration and recognition from colleagues. Share credit and take a moment to enjoy it. Reversed, you may feel disconnected from your team, or a launch might be delayed. Strengthen the basics. Appreciate the people who helped you get here.
finances: Financially, the Four of Wands points to stability and a sense of security, possibly through shared resources or a property matter. It is a reasonable time to celebrate goals reached while still budgeting wisely. Reversed, you might feel unsettled about household money or a shared expense that needs open discussion.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests that connection and celebration are good for you. Time with people you trust, shared meals or a pleasant gathering can lift your mood. A steady home routine may help. Reversed, loneliness or household stress could weigh on you. A professional can offer support if needed.
advice: Mark the milestone and let people share it with you. Strengthen the foundations that made this moment possible.
as_feelings: They may feel at ease and happy around you, picturing shared occasions and a settled bond. There could be a wish to include you in their circle. Their feelings are likely warm and steady rather than stormy. They may be hoping for stability.

name: Five of Wands
summary: Competing voices and clashing ideas create noise and friction, which can sharpen you if the struggle stays honest.
imagery: Five young figures in mismatched clothing hold wooden staffs and seem to swing them at one another on open, uneven ground. Nobody appears badly hurt, and nobody is clearly winning. The colours of their clothes clash, as do their ideas. Behind them is a plain, bright sky. The scene resembles a rough game or a chaotic argument more than a real battle, showing energy spent without a common goal or an agreed rule.
upright: The Five of Wands describes a scene of competition and disagreement, usually more messy than dangerous. You may be in a crowded room of opinions, a team where everyone wants to lead, or a situation where you are fighting for attention. The figures in the card all have staffs and all have energy, but none are working together. This can feel exhausting, yet it often has a useful side. Friction can test your ideas, show where your argument is weak and push you to improve. Healthy competition can sharpen skills, while unhealthy conflict wastes effort. Ask whether the struggle serves a purpose or whether it is just noise. You might need to state your position more clearly, set ground rules or decide which battles are worth your effort. Pay attention to ego, both yours and other people's. If you can move from everyone shouting to everyone playing by the same rules, the energy becomes productive.
reversed: Reversed, the Five of Wands can mean that conflict is easing, or that you are avoiding it. You may be finding a truce, reaching a compromise or deciding that a particular fight is no longer worth your energy. That is often a healthy sign. It can also describe tension that is being suppressed rather than resolved, so things look calm while resentment simmers below. If you avoid every disagreement, important issues may stay unaddressed. Another meaning involves inner conflict, where your own competing wants pull you in different directions and leave you drained. Take a look at which meaning feels true. If a fight is ending, allow it to end gracefully and refuse to keep score. If you have been holding your tongue, consider a calm, direct conversation. Disagreement handled with respect can strengthen a relationship or a team.
love: In love, the Five of Wands suggests bickering, friction or competing needs. Two strong personalities may be clashing, or a third party might cause tension. It can also be a playful, spirited dynamic when kept light. Talk about what you each need rather than debating who is right. Reversed, you may be settling an argument or avoiding one that needs attention. Playful rivalry can add spark, as long as neither of you feels truly dismissed or unheard.
career: At work, this card points to competition, crowded meetings and clashing opinions. You might be vying for a role or caught between colleagues with different approaches. Stay clear about your contribution and look for shared goals. Reversed, conflict may settle, or you may be avoiding a needed discussion. Choose your battles carefully. A clear conversation with a manager about roles and expectations may reduce the friction.
finances: Financially, the Five of Wands may show competition for resources, disagreements over shared money or a crowded market. Keep your expenses and agreements clear. Reversed, a dispute may be resolved, or avoidance may be hiding an issue that deserves a closer look before it grows. Written agreements and clear records help prevent misunderstandings.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests that stress and inner tension may be affecting you. Physical activity, especially play or sport, can help release restless energy. Reversed, you may be pushing feelings down. Speak with a professional if tension is persistent or overwhelming.
advice: Decide which disagreements deserve your energy and drop the rest. Turn noise into a clear conversation with shared rules.
as_feelings: They may feel competitive, restless or unsure how to handle the tension between you. Some of the friction could be a sign of strong feeling expressed awkwardly. They might be confused about where they stand and reacting with edge instead of openness.

name: Six of Wands
summary: A win is being acknowledged, and the card invites you to accept praise with confidence while staying grounded.
imagery: A rider on a white horse moves through a crowd, wearing a laurel wreath on their head and holding a staff topped with a victory wreath. The horse is draped in green. Five other staffs are carried by people on foot, who look up at the rider with admiration. The sky is pale and clear. The mood is that of a parade after a hard-won achievement, with the winner carried forward by the goodwill of the people around them.
upright: The Six of Wands celebrates success that others can see. You may have finished a difficult project, passed an exam, received a promotion or simply overcome something that tested you. The rider is honoured by a crowd, which reminds you that victory feels richer when it is shared and witnessed. This card encourages you to accept recognition without shrinking from it. You earned this attention through effort, and acknowledging it can strengthen your confidence for the next challenge. It also reminds you that the people walking beside the rider helped create the moment, so thanks and credit are worth giving. Public support, good news and a rise in reputation are all possible themes. At the same time, the rider stays on the horse, and the crowd's mood can change. Enjoy the praise, yet keep your eyes forward and your humility intact. Success is a fine place to rest briefly, though not to stop growing. Let your win become a base for your next goal rather than a final destination.
reversed: Reversed, the Six of Wands may point to success that feels hollow or recognition that has not come. You might have worked hard without receiving credit, or you may have achieved something and found it less satisfying than expected. The card can also describe pride that has grown too large, where the need for admiration begins to shape your choices. In some readings, it warns of a public stumble or a loss of confidence after a setback. Ask what kind of recognition you truly want, and from whom. Praise from people whose opinion you respect often matters more than a large crowd. If you are overlooked, state your contribution clearly instead of waiting for others to notice. If you are the one who is basking, check whether you are leaving others behind. A quiet private victory may still be real, even when nobody applauds.
love: In love, the Six of Wands suggests pride in your relationship or feeling confident and attractive. You may be happy to be seen with a partner, or a connection may be validated by friends and family. If you are single, your self-assurance could draw attention. Celebrate each other's wins. Reversed, you may feel unappreciated, or ego and comparison could be affecting the bond. Being proud of each other can deepen trust, so say it out loud.
career: At work, this card points to recognition, a promotion, a successful presentation or a project that earns real praise. Your effort is being seen. Share credit with your team and use the confidence to aim higher. Reversed, you may feel overlooked, or a win might not carry the reward you hoped for. Speak up about your contribution. Let your results speak while staying kind.
finances: Financially, the Six of Wands suggests rewards from past effort, such as a bonus, a successful deal or progress toward a goal. Enjoy it sensibly and avoid overspending to display success. Reversed, expected returns may fall short, or the urge to impress may influence your spending in ways you later regret.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests that confidence and a sense of achievement can lift your mood. Celebrate a health milestone you have reached, large or small. Reversed, you may feel discouraged or overly self-critical. Consider talking to a professional if low confidence lingers.
advice: Let yourself receive the praise, then thank those who helped you. Keep building on this win instead of resting on it.
as_feelings: They may admire you and feel proud of how you carry yourself. There could be a wish to be seen with you or to earn your respect. Their feelings might include some competitiveness, though the admiration looks genuine. They may also want your approval.

name: Seven of Wands
summary: You hold a position worth defending, and steady courage matters more than winning every argument.
imagery: A figure stands on a hilltop holding a wooden staff, with six other staffs rising from below as if reaching up to challenge them. The figure wears mismatched boots, one of which does not match the other, hinting at a hasty readiness. The ground is high and green, and the sky is clear. They look downward at their opponents with a focused, determined expression, having the advantage of height but no chance to relax.
upright: The Seven of Wands shows someone defending ground they have earned. You may be challenged on your opinions, your work, your boundaries or your place in a group. The figure on the hill has the advantage of height, which suggests that you are in a stronger position than you feel. The mismatched boots hint that you may be caught off guard, yet you are still standing. This card asks for courage and consistency. You do not need to win every argument or crush every opposing voice. You need to know what you stand for and hold it calmly. Ask which challenges are worth the effort and which are distractions. Sometimes the best defence is a clear boundary delivered without heat. Be ready to adjust if you meet a valid point, because standing your ground does not mean refusing to listen. The pressure may feel constant, but it often reveals how much you believe in your position. Keep your footing, breathe, and trust the strength you have built.
reversed: Reversed, the Seven of Wands can mean you are tired of defending yourself. You may feel overwhelmed by criticism, outnumbered by demands, or ready to drop the staff altogether. Giving up can be wise if the fight is no longer yours, though it can also be a retreat made too early from exhaustion. The card sometimes warns of defensiveness that has gone too far, where every comment feels like an attack and you meet it with more force than needed. Notice whether the threat is real or whether you are reacting to old wounds. Rest and support matter here. You do not have to hold the hill alone, and asking for help is a sign of good judgement. Decide what is truly worth protecting and let go of the remainder. A clear, calm no or a boundary stated once may do more than constant vigilance ever could.
love: In love, the Seven of Wands suggests defending a relationship or your own needs within it. Outside opinions, jealousy or a rival may put pressure on you. Stay calm, communicate your boundaries and avoid reacting out of insecurity. Reversed, you may be worn out by the effort, or defensive habits could be keeping closeness at a distance. Notice whether you are defending your partner or defending your pride, because the two call for very different responses.
career: At work, this card points to competition, criticism or a need to defend your ideas and position. You may be challenged, and you have solid ground if you stay prepared. Back up your claims with facts and remain composed. Reversed, you might feel burned out, outnumbered or tempted to yield too quickly. Choose the criticisms worth answering and let the rest pass without reply.
finances: Financially, the Seven of Wands suggests protecting what you have built and standing firm in negotiations. Know your limits and do not be pressured into rash decisions. Reversed, financial strain may feel heavy, and you could be tempted to give up on a plan too soon. Seek advice from someone you trust.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests that stress and constant vigilance may be wearing on you. Rest, boundaries and calming activities could help. Reversed, you may feel drained and in need of support. If stress feels overwhelming, consider speaking with a health professional.
advice: Stand by what matters to you and let the minor skirmishes go. Hold your boundary calmly, and ask for support if you need it.
as_feelings: They may feel defensive or under pressure when they think of you. There could be a wish to protect what is between you, or a sense of being challenged by outside opinions. Their feelings may be strong but guarded. They might show it as sharpness.

name: Eight of Wands
summary: Things speed up, with news, travel or decisions arriving quickly, so stay alert and keep your aim steady.
imagery: Eight wooden staffs fly diagonally through a clear blue sky, all pointing the same direction and nearly parallel. There are no people in the picture. Below, a river winds through a green landscape with a few distant hills. The staffs are about to land, or perhaps they are still in flight. The scene feels light and quick, a moment of pure motion where everything seems aligned and headed toward its destination.
upright: The Eight of Wands is the card of momentum. After the waiting and tension of earlier cards, things suddenly move, and they may move fast. You might receive news, a message, an offer or a flurry of activity that carries you forward. Travel and quick communication are also traditional associations. The staffs are all aimed the same way, which suggests that your energy and circumstances are well aligned. This is a good moment to act decisively, reply promptly and take advantage of a rapid opening. At the same time, speed requires attention, since things landing quickly may need quick handling. Keep your focus and avoid scattering your attention across too many directions. Prepare yourself for a busier stretch, and trust that progress is possible. The card also shows the pleasure of being unblocked, when a slow situation finally clears. Enjoy the sense of flow, and be ready to catch what arrives, because these opportunities tend to pass through quickly rather than lingering.
reversed: Reversed, the Eight of Wands may describe delays, crossed wires or energy that cannot find a direction. A message may be late, a plan might stall, or things could be moving so fast that you cannot think clearly. You may also feel scattered, taking on too many tasks and finishing none of them. Sometimes the card suggests that you are rushing and need to slow down to avoid mistakes. At other times it shows an obstacle in the path that is holding back progress through no fault of your own. Check your communication, confirm details and give yourself time to respond properly. If the pace is too frantic, choose one priority and let secondary matters wait. If things are too slow, look for what is blocking the line. Patience may be difficult, but the momentum is usually still there beneath the delay, ready to return once the interference is cleared.
love: In love, the Eight of Wands suggests quick developments, such as fast messages, a sudden invitation or a connection that moves ahead rapidly. Passion may flare, and you might feel carried along. Keep honest communication close while things are moving. Reversed, mixed messages, delays or a rush toward commitment may need a gentler pace. Replies may arrive faster than expected, and a short trip or a spontaneous meeting could bring you together sooner than planned.
career: At work, this card points to fast progress, speedy communication and projects gaining momentum. News, emails, travel or a sudden deadline may fill your days. Stay organised and respond promptly. Reversed, you may face delays, miscommunication or overwork. Prioritise a few tasks and confirm details before moving on. Keep a clear list of priorities, since requests may arrive quickly and several at once.
finances: Financially, the Eight of Wands suggests money or opportunities moving quickly, such as a fast sale, a quick payment or a speedy decision. Read details before you commit. Reversed, delays in payments or hasty choices may cause trouble. Slow down and double-check figures before you act. Keep records of anything agreed.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests lots of energy and a desire to move, which may suit active routines. Take care that a busy pace does not leave you frazzled. Reversed, you may feel scattered or rushed. If constant speed leaves you unwell, rest and speak to a professional.
advice: Act promptly while the path is open, and keep your focus on one clear direction. Confirm details before you move fast.
as_feelings: They may feel a sudden rush of interest and want to move things along. Messages or contact from them could arrive quickly. Their eagerness might be real, though the speed may leave them unsure where it is heading. Their contact may come in bursts.

name: Nine of Wands
summary: You are wounded but still standing, and one last push of resilience may be what finishes the journey.
imagery: A bandaged figure stands with a head wrapped in a white cloth, leaning on a wooden staff while keeping a wary eye to one side. Behind them, eight more staffs stand upright in a line like a fence. The background is pale and bare. The figure looks tired yet watchful, showing someone who has been through repeated challenges and is determined not to give up, even though caution has become a habit.
upright: The Nine of Wands appears when you have been through a lot and you are nearly at the end. You may be tired, a little bruised and wary of the next disappointment. The bandaged figure shows that you carry the marks of earlier struggles, and the line of staffs behind them shows how much you have already survived. This card honours persistence. You are closer to the goal than you may feel, and strength is still in reserve. At the same time, it invites you to notice how wariness has shaped you. Some caution is wise, but constant suspicion can wear you out. Ask whether you are still guarding against a threat that has passed. You might need rest, a boundary or a smaller load so you can make the final push with a clear head. Do not mistake tiredness for failure. Lean on the staff, accept help if it is offered and keep going with patience. The last stretch often asks for steadiness more than speed.
reversed: Reversed, the Nine of Wands can show burnout, stubbornness or a refusal to put down a burden that no longer serves you. You may be so used to bracing for the next blow that you cannot relax even when things are quiet. The card can describe suspicion that colours every new situation, or a sense that you have nothing left to give. It may also warn against pushing through when rest is truly needed. Take the signals your body and mind are sending. Giving yourself time to heal is not a surrender. Look at which walls you have built, and ask whether some can come down, especially around people who have shown they are safe. If you have been carrying everything alone, consider sharing the load. Sometimes the bravest step is to stop defending and begin recovering, so that you can return to the goal in better shape.
love: In love, the Nine of Wands suggests guardedness after past hurt. You may be wary of trusting again, or a relationship may be recovering from a difficult period. Go gently and share your fears honestly. Reversed, defensiveness or fear of being hurt may keep a potential partner at a distance. Trust returns through small, consistent acts rather than big declarations, so allow time and notice who stays steady when things get difficult.
career: At work, this card points to being close to a finish line after a long effort. You may be tired but capable. Pace yourself and finish what matters. Reversed, burnout, stubborn overwork or a sense that nothing will change may be present. Rest, ask for support and reconsider your load. A final deadline or review may be close, so keep your focus and protect your remaining energy.
finances: Financially, the Nine of Wands suggests perseverance through a tight stretch and being close to a recovery. Stay careful with your resources without letting fear drive every choice. Reversed, worry may be consuming you, or exhaustion may push you toward giving up on a plan that still has potential. Keep a small reserve.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests you may be tired and in need of rest and recovery. Listen to your body and pace yourself. Reversed, burnout may be near. Please speak to a health professional if exhaustion or constant tension persists, and consider asking for practical help.
advice: You are closer to the end than you feel, so rest where you can and take the last stretch steadily. Let someone share the load.
as_feelings: They may feel cautious and protective of themselves, perhaps because of past hurt. There could be real feelings underneath, held back by fear of being let down. They might need time and reassurance to lower their guard. They may test your steadiness first.

name: Ten of Wands
summary: You are carrying a heavy load, and the card asks whether all of it is truly yours to hold.
imagery: A figure bends forward under the weight of ten wooden staffs bundled in their arms, so that their face is hidden behind the load. They walk along a path toward a village visible in the distance, where houses with lit windows wait on the horizon. The field beside them is ploughed and the sky is a warm ochre. The destination is near, yet the effort looks heavy and the figure cannot see what is directly ahead.
upright: The Ten of Wands shows a time when responsibility has grown heavy. You may have said yes to too many things, taken on a project that expanded, or inherited tasks that were never fully yours. The figure carries every staff alone, even though the village is close, and that detail matters. The finish line is near, yet the load makes it hard to see. This card often arrives when you are working hard and feel stretched, but it also asks you to look at how the burden was gathered. Some of it may be a commitment you chose with pride. Some may be habits like perfectionism or difficulty saying no. Ask what can be put down, shared or delayed. Not every staff needs to be carried at once. Reaching the village matters more than proving you can bear everything. Support, prioritising and honest limits are good tools now. The weight is real, and so is your determination, so aim to keep the second without sacrificing your wellbeing for it.
reversed: Reversed, the Ten of Wands can mean that a burden is lifting, or that it has become too much. You might be learning to delegate, set limits or admit that a role is not yours to keep. That is a relief worth welcoming. The card can also describe a breaking point, where overwork leads to exhaustion, resentment or a collapse of the plan. If you notice that you are close to this, treat the warning seriously. Consider which responsibilities truly belong to you and which have drifted your way because you are reliable. Ask for help clearly, and accept that it may not be done exactly as you would have done it. Putting down a few staffs does not make you weak. It may let you see the road ahead and arrive with energy left.
love: In love, the Ten of Wands suggests that responsibilities may be crowding out connection. You may carry most of the emotional or practical load in a relationship, leading to tiredness or resentment. Share the weight and speak about what you need. Reversed, a burden may ease, or the strain may call for honest change. Small gestures of help, such as sharing chores or planning time together, can restore balance and warmth between you.
career: At work, this card points to overload, long hours and too many responsibilities landing on you. You are close to completion, but the cost is high. Prioritise, delegate and say no where you can. Reversed, you may be releasing tasks, or you might be nearing burnout and need a change of pace. Check which tasks truly require your skills and which could be passed on.
finances: Financially, the Ten of Wands suggests heavy obligations, debts or a sense of carrying a household's costs alone. Review where money is going and what can be reduced or shared. Reversed, a financial burden may be easing, or strain may be reaching a point that calls for outside advice. Seek a trusted view.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests that stress and overwork may be taking a toll. Rest, shared tasks and gentle routines can help. Reversed, your body may be asking you to stop. If tiredness or tension is persistent, please speak with a health professional.
advice: Put down what is not yours and ask someone to carry part of the rest. The journey does not have to be solitary.
as_feelings: They may feel overloaded and unsure how to make space for you. Their feelings could be real but buried under duties and stress. They might be reaching for relief and wishing for ease between you. They may long for a lighter, easier time with you.

name: Page of Wands
summary: A curious messenger arrives with exciting news, inviting you to explore a new idea with a beginner's openness.
imagery: A young figure in a yellow tunic decorated with small salamander shapes stands in a barren desert landscape, holding a tall wooden staff with fresh leaves. Their hat carries a feather, and they gaze at the top of the staff with curiosity. Behind them lie pyramids and a few dry hills under a pale sky. The salamanders hint at fire, and the lone traveller seems eager to explore the unknown.
upright: The Page of Wands is an enthusiastic beginner, bright with curiosity and ready to try something new. This card often points to a message, idea or invitation that gets your attention and makes you want to explore. It may be news about a creative project, a learning opportunity or a chance to do something that feels fun and a little daring. The page looks at the staff as though it holds a question. That suggests openness more than expertise. You do not need to know everything to start. The card also describes a person, perhaps young or young at heart, who is adventurous, direct and full of fresh ideas. Notice what draws your interest without any obvious reason. Follow it with a playful attitude, take notes and test it in small ways. Treat this as the beginning of a new chapter, and let your questions lead the way.
reversed: Reversed, the Page of Wands may suggest that enthusiasm is scattered or that you are jumping into things without a plan. You may start many projects and finish few, or you may feel restless without a clear direction. The card can describe immaturity, such as acting on impulse, boasting about plans or avoiding the unglamorous parts of a task. Sometimes the news you hoped for is delayed or turns out to be less exciting than promised. It may also mean that fear of looking foolish is keeping your curiosity under wraps. Consider where your energy is going and what deserves a more focused commitment. Choose one idea and give it a defined amount of time before you add another. If you feel stuck, take a lighter approach, such as a short experiment, to rebuild your sense of play. Enthusiasm grows stronger when it is matched by follow-through.
love: In love, the Page of Wands suggests a playful, exciting new interest, perhaps a flirtatious message or a fresh crush. It can also mean enjoying the early, curious phase of dating. Keep things light and honest. Reversed, mixed signals, immaturity or a lack of follow-through may leave you unsure what the other person wants. If you have been seeing someone, a new activity together could revive the early thrill and bring out playful sides of you both.
career: At work, this card points to a new idea, a learning opportunity or an exciting message about a project. You may be exploring a different field or trying a creative approach. Stay open and experiment. Reversed, you may feel unfocused, or an idea may need more planning before it can succeed. A short course or a creative side project could point to something bigger.
finances: Financially, the Page of Wands suggests a new idea for earning, or an opportunity to learn a money skill. Start small and treat it as an experiment. Reversed, impulsive spending or an undeveloped scheme may cause problems, so research before committing funds to something exciting. Keep early spending modest and track results.
health: For wellbeing, this card encourages trying a new activity that feels fun, like a dance class or a different kind of walk. Curiosity can bring energy. Reversed, you may start routines and drop them quickly. Be patient, and speak to a professional if you need tailored guidance.
advice: Follow your curiosity and try a small experiment this week. Keep the beginner's lightness, and add one piece of follow-through.
as_feelings: They may feel excited and curious about you, with a playful side showing. There could be a wish to explore the connection without heavy expectations. Their interest may be genuine but still young and easily distracted. They may enjoy teasing and light messages.

name: Knight of Wands
astrology: Fire of Fire, 20 degrees Scorpio to 20 degrees Sagittarius
summary: Bold, passionate energy sweeps in, bringing adventure and momentum, though it asks for some direction to avoid recklessness.
imagery: A knight in armour with a plumed helmet sits on a rearing chestnut horse, holding a leafy wooden staff. Their yellow tunic, like the page's, is decorated with salamanders, and a red cloak flows behind. The desert landscape behind them is dry, with pyramids on the horizon. The horse seems eager to run, and the rider looks ahead with confidence, showing a drive to rush toward goals without waiting.
upright: The Knight of Wands arrives with speed, charisma and a hunger for adventure. This card often signals a burst of action, such as a sudden decision to travel, a quick start on a project or a surge of passion toward a goal. It may also describe a person who is confident, daring and fun, someone who lives boldly and inspires others to do the same. The rearing horse suggests a lot of power that needs good handling. You may feel eager to charge forward, and in many cases that confidence will serve you well. This card asks you to move, to try and to follow your enthusiasm. It also asks you to bring some awareness along. Fast action works best when it has a destination. Notice whether you are heading toward something you want or just away from boredom. Channel the heat into a goal and keep your promises, since your energy can impress others and also leave them behind.
reversed: Reversed, the Knight of Wands can describe impulsiveness that causes trouble. You might rush into a plan without preparation, lose interest as soon as it gets difficult, or spread yourself across too many exciting ideas. The card can also point to a person who makes bold promises and fails to follow through, or to a temper that flares quickly. Sometimes it indicates delays and frustration, as though the horse is held back and stamping. Look for where your energy is being wasted, and ask what would help you pace yourself. Slow down enough to consider consequences, especially in decisions that affect others. If you are burned out from sprinting, rest without guilt. If you feel stalled, look at what you are afraid of, because anxiety can hide behind restlessness. Reversed, this knight suggests that passion needs structure, and that finishing something can be more satisfying than starting ten things.
love: In love, the Knight of Wands suggests a passionate, exciting romance, often with a strong first spark and a love of adventure. It can also describe a charming but restless partner. Enjoy the intensity while paying attention to consistency. Reversed, hot-and-cold behaviour or a quick fling that fades may cause confusion. Make sure the passion is matched by kindness and reliability, and be clear about what you each want before things move too fast.
career: At work, this card points to bold moves, a fast-paced project or an ambitious push toward a goal. You may be drawn to travel or a daring venture. Keep your plans organised so energy converts into results. Reversed, impulsive choices, overpromising or burnout may be getting in the way. Clear milestones and regular check-ins can help turn that enthusiasm into steady, reliable progress.
finances: Financially, the Knight of Wands suggests a willingness to take risks or invest in an exciting opportunity. Be bold while still checking the numbers. Reversed, rash spending, hasty investments or lack of follow-through could create trouble. Slow down and consider long-term effects before you commit. Set a limit before you act.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests high energy and a need for active outlets such as sport or travel. Warm up and pace yourself to avoid overdoing it. Reversed, you may be burning out or acting recklessly. Rest matters, and a health professional can give personal advice.
advice: Give your energy a direction and move toward it with confidence. Slow down just enough to think about who you are bringing along.
as_feelings: They may feel intensely drawn to you and eager to act on it. There could be bold gestures or sudden plans. Their enthusiasm may be strong, though they could lose focus if things slow down. They may find it hard to sit still with feelings.

name: Queen of Wands
astrology: Water of Fire, 20 degrees Pisces to 20 degrees Aries
summary: Warm, confident and self-assured, the Queen of Wands invites you to lead with your passion and welcome others in.
imagery: A queen sits on a throne decorated with lions and sunflowers, holding a wooden staff in one hand and a single sunflower in the other. Her yellow gown is vivid, and she gazes calmly to one side. A black cat sits at her feet, and the landscape beyond is dry with pyramids and mountains. The lions suggest strength, the sunflower suggests warmth and growth, and the cat adds a hint of independence and intuition.
upright: The Queen of Wands is vibrant, confident and at ease with her own presence. This card may describe a quality in you or a person around you who radiates warmth and draws others in. She knows what she wants, and she works toward it with courage and charm. The sunflower and the lions show that she combines gentle growth with real strength. She is not afraid to be seen, and she inspires people through enthusiasm rather than force. When she appears, it may be time to step into your own confidence, take up space and share your talents. Let your passion be visible. This card also encourages generosity, since a good fire warms everyone near it. She is independent and values her freedom, so you might look for ways to keep your autonomy while still connecting with others. Follow what you love, host the gathering or lead the project. Trust that your authentic enthusiasm will be felt and appreciated, even if you do not feel entirely ready.
reversed: Reversed, the Queen of Wands can show a dimming of confidence or a flare of jealousy. You might feel insecure, compare yourself with others or hold back your own light. The card may also describe a demanding, controlling attitude, such as needing to be the centre of attention or reacting sharply when criticised. Sometimes it signals burnout from giving too much energy to everyone else. Think about what is eating at your sense of self-worth, and who or what is draining your fire. Insecurity often hides behind a loud front, so be gentle with yourself as you look. Rest and reconnect with the things that made you feel alive. If you notice petty rivalry or sharp words, take a breath and speak from honesty instead. Your warmth has not vanished. It may simply need a moment of care and a little more trust in your own worth.
love: In love, the Queen of Wands suggests a passionate, loyal and confident approach. You or your partner may bring warmth, humour and independence to the bond. If you are single, being yourself openly is attractive. Reversed, jealousy, possessiveness or insecurity may need honest attention. She is attracted to honesty and loyalty, and she gives them in return. Let yourself be seen without performing, and invite your partner to do the same.
career: At work, this card points to leadership, charisma and the ability to inspire a team. You may be well suited to a visible role or a creative venture. Lead with warmth and clarity. Reversed, ego clashes, self-doubt or burnout could hinder progress, so recover your confidence before you take on more. Your presence can motivate others, so share your ideas openly in meetings.
finances: Financially, the Queen of Wands suggests confident, independent money management and the drive to build your own income. Back your abilities and plan well. Reversed, overspending to impress or insecurity about money may be shaping your choices. Return to a simple budget and trust gradual progress. Trust your own judgement, and review it regularly.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests vitality, a strong sense of self and a need for activities you enjoy. Dance, sunshine and social movement may suit you. Reversed, you may feel drained or self-critical. Be gentle with yourself and consult a professional if low mood persists.
advice: Show up as yourself and let your warmth lead. Protect your energy so you can keep sharing it.
as_feelings: They may feel drawn to your confidence and enjoy being near your energy. There could be admiration mixed with a wish to impress you. Their feelings are likely warm, direct and open, with some pride in the mix. They may be a little nervous too.

name: King of Wands
astrology: Air of Fire, 20 degrees Cancer to 20 degrees Leo
summary: A natural leader with vision and drive, the King of Wands asks you to guide others with honour and clear purpose.
imagery: A king sits on a throne carved with lions and salamanders, holding a flowering wooden staff and wearing a red cloak over a yellow tunic. A small salamander appears at his feet, and the background is a deep orange sky over mountains. His gaze is steady and his posture relaxed but alert. Everything about the image suggests command that comes from experience, a leader who has mastered his own fire and uses it to guide others.
upright: The King of Wands is the visionary leader who turns ideas into action. He has the passion of the earlier cards, now refined by experience, and he knows how to channel it. This card may describe your own leadership qualities or a person in your life who inspires through vision, honour and confidence. It often appears when you are ready to take charge of a project, build something ambitious or make bold decisions with a clear sense of purpose. The salamander and lions show a mastered fire, one that no longer burns wildly but warms and drives. You may be asked to speak up for what you believe, to guide a group or to take responsibility for a plan from beginning to end. Lead by example rather than demand. Share your vision in a way that invites others to join, and listen to the people whose skills complement yours. Authority works best when it is backed by integrity. Trust your instincts, plan with long-term thinking and act with generosity.
reversed: Reversed, the King of Wands may suggest that leadership has slipped into domination or impulsive decision-making. You may be tempted to push others toward your vision without listening, or to promise more than can be delivered. The card can describe someone arrogant, hot-tempered or more interested in being admired than in doing the work. It may also point to a leader whose confidence is shaky beneath a loud exterior, or to your own doubts when you are asked to guide others. Check whether you are leaving people behind in your hurry. Slow down enough to listen and weigh the facts before acting. If you are working under a difficult authority, protect your boundaries and look for support. Reversed, this king invites you to examine your motives and remember that real strength includes humility and the willingness to change course.
love: In love, the King of Wands suggests a confident, loyal and passionate partner, or showing those qualities yourself. A relationship may benefit from a shared vision and bold plans. Make room for your partner's voice. Reversed, controlling behaviour, ego or a need to dominate may cause strain. This king values honour and commitment, so loyalty and honest talk about the future matter. Be generous with praise and make space for your partner's wishes as well as your own.
career: At work, this card points to leadership, entrepreneurship and the ability to turn a vision into reality. You may be ready to take charge, start a venture or guide a team. Be clear and inspiring. Reversed, overbearing management, unrealistic goals or hasty decisions may undermine the project. Delegate wisely, back your people and keep your promises so that your authority is respected rather than feared.
finances: Financially, the King of Wands suggests confident, strategic decisions and a talent for building wealth through bold but considered ventures. Think long term and take advice. Reversed, overconfidence or impulsive investment may cause losses. Review the risks and set realistic expectations. Think in years rather than weeks, and keep some reserves for the unexpected.
health: For wellbeing, this card suggests strong vitality and the drive to lead a healthy lifestyle. Keep a balanced routine so ambition does not crowd out rest. Reversed, you might push too hard or ignore warning signs. A health professional can help you find a sustainable pace.
advice: Lead with a clear vision and a listening ear. Let your confidence invite others in rather than overrule them.
as_feelings: They may feel admiring and respectful of you, with a wish to be a strong presence in your life. There could be pride and a desire to protect or guide. Their feelings are likely steady and committed, though they may be used to taking the lead.

name: Ace of Cups
summary: Your heart opens to a fresh wave of feeling, creativity or connection, and the gift is offered freely.
imagery: A hand reaches out from a cloud and holds a golden cup. A white dove descends toward it with a small wafer marked with a cross, and five streams of water pour from the cup into a pond covered with lotus flowers. Water droplets fall like blessings. The scene is calm and bright, suggesting that love and spirit arrive as a gift and that the cup is already full enough to overflow.
upright: The Ace of Cups brings a feeling of emotional beginnings. Something in your heart opens, whether it is a new relationship, a deeper friendship, a creative impulse or a quiet sense of peace you had not felt for a while. The cup overflows without effort, which suggests that this kind of love does not need to be forced. It simply asks to be received. You might notice greater empathy, a longing to connect or a sudden clarity about what you value. This card often appears when old hurt starts to soften and you become willing to feel again. It can also point to spiritual renewal and intuition that feels warm rather than anxious. Allow yourself to accept kindness, and let your own compassion show. Not every gift becomes a lasting commitment, yet this one deserves to be welcomed with an open heart. Take a moment to notice what fills you. Share the feeling, make something from it and be gentle with how new and tender it may be.
reversed: Reversed, the Ace of Cups can suggest that the cup is blocked or tipped over. You may be holding back feelings because you fear being hurt, or you may feel emotionally flat, as if nothing reaches you. Sometimes the card describes a missed or delayed connection, a love offered at a bad time or a creative flow that dries up when you criticise it too harshly. It can also show that you pour so much into others that nothing remains for yourself. Look at what has made your heart feel unsafe, and whether the wall you built is still necessary. Emotions that are ignored tend to return in other ways, so give them a gentle outlet through writing, art or quiet reflection. The water is still there. It may only need a clearer channel, and some patience while you learn to trust it again.
love: In love, the Ace of Cups is one of the most hopeful cards. It can point to a new romance, a deepening of an existing bond or a sudden sense of emotional closeness. If you are single, you may be ready for love in a way that feels genuine rather than rushed. In a relationship, it may bring tenderness and renewed affection. Reversed, hurt or fear may keep your heart closed for now.
career: At work, this card suggests a role or project that feels meaningful, or a creative idea that touches you. You may find satisfaction through helping others or working with people you care about. Follow what feels emotionally right as well as practical. Reversed, you may feel uninspired, unappreciated or disconnected from the purpose behind what you do. Let that care show in your work.
finances: Financially, the Ace of Cups is less about numbers and more about attitude. It can suggest a gift, a generous gesture or work you love that also supports you. Spend in ways that reflect your values. Reversed, emotional spending or a lack of fulfilment around money may be at play, so check in with your real needs.
health: For wellbeing, this card points to emotional refreshment and the benefits of rest, water and gentle self-compassion. Time near a lake or a warm bath may soothe you. Reversed, suppressed feelings could weigh on you. If sadness lingers, consider speaking with a counsellor or doctor.
advice: Let yourself receive kindness and feel what rises. Share the warmth with someone, even in a small way.
as_feelings: They may feel a soft, genuine openness toward you, with affection beginning to show. Their heart may be willing, even if they are still sorting out what the feeling means. They could be moved by kindness and eager to share something sincere.

name: Two of Cups
summary: Two people meet with mutual respect and warmth, forming a bond built on giving and receiving in equal measure.
imagery: A man and a woman face each other, each holding a cup and exchanging them or lifting them in a pledge. Both wear wreaths, and the space between them holds a caduceus topped with a winged lion's head. Behind them stands a small house on a hill. The two stand evenly and look directly at one another, showing a meeting of equals in which each person offers something and accepts something in return.
